newsitem.title: NORWAY: European markets take shine off Norwegian shares.
newsitem.headline: European markets take shine off Norwegian shares.

text.p: Norwegian shares opened in a bullish mood and hit new intraday peaks before jittery overseas markets, especially France, took the steam out of the rally.
Dealers said sentiment on the Oslo bourse was positive, but expectations lay between a flat market or a slight correction due to outside influences.
"There's still a lot of cash in the market. The companies are paying out dividends and that makes the mutual funds very liquid and that money has to be invested," said one broker.
The Total share index closed a marginal 0.27 percent up at 1,166.59 points, having hit a high at 1,173.92 points.
Total turnover amounted to 1.2 billion crowns.

Telecommunications company Nera once again gained strongly in relatively heavy trade of 81 million crowns as investors continued to be impressed by positive analysts' reports. Nera advanced 2.72 percent to 41.60 crowns.
Trade also was brisk in Saga Petroluem, which is due to post first four-month results on Thursday. The stock gained three crowns, or 2.15 percent, to 142.50 crowns.
A Reuter poll of nine analysts forecast Norway's largest listed oil company to post pre-tax profits for the tertial at 456 million crowns and opeating profits of 1.42 billion crowns.
